recipes.name: Surmai (Kingfish/Mackerel) Curry with Brown Rice
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids from the fatty fish, which may help support healthy cholesterol levels and reduce triglycerides. It also provides Vitamin D, crucial for bone health and immune function, addressing your low Vitamin D biomarker. Brown rice adds beneficial fiber.
instructions: Wash and marinate fish with a pinch of turmeric and salt. Set aside.
Cook brown rice according to package instructions.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add curry leaves and green chilies. Sauté for a minute.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add coconut milk and kudampuli/tamarind paste. Bring to a simmer.
Gently add the marinated fish pieces. Cover and cook for 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Oats and Vegetable Uttapam
recipes.health_benefit: Oats are an excellent source of soluble fiber, particularly beta-glucan, which is known to help lower LDL cholesterol by reducing its absorption. The addition of vegetables boosts nutrient and fiber content, contributing to heart health.
instructions: Dry roast oats lightly and grind them into a coarse flour. Mix with sooji in a bowl.
Add curd and enough water to make a smooth batter of pouring consistency, similar to dosa batter. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes.
Add chopped onion, tomato, capsicum, green chili, coriander leaves, and salt to the batter. Mix well.
If using, add fruit salt or baking soda just before cooking and mix gently.
Heat a non-stick griddle. Pour a ladleful of batter and spread it slightly thick into a circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edges.
Cook on medium heat until golden brown on one side, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal (Red Lentil) with Spinach and Whole Wheat Roti
recipes.health_benefit: Lentils are an excellent source of soluble fiber, which can help lower LDL cholesterol. Spinach adds vitamins, minerals, and more fiber, supporting overall cardiovascular health. Whole wheat roti provides complex carbohydrates and fiber.
instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and soak for 15-20 minutes. Drain and cook with 1.5 cups water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt until soft (approx. 10-15 mins). Mash lightly.
Prepare dough for rotis: mix whole wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt. Knead until smooth. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and asafoetida. Once spluttering, add chopped onion and green chili. Sauté until onion is translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander, and cumin powders. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add chopped spinach and cook until wilted.
Stir in the cooked dal. Add water to adjust consistency if needed. Bring to a simmer.
Add garam masala and fresh coriander. Check seasoning.
Roll out rotis from the whole wheat dough and cook on a griddle until puffed and cooked.
Serve hot dal with whole wheat rotis.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Salad with Chicken Chunks
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong beans are packed with fiber, which is beneficial for managing LDL cholesterol, and provide easily digestible plant protein. The lean chicken adds complete protein, making it a satisfying and nutrient-dense snack that supports overall health.
instructions: If not pre-sprouted, soak moong beans overnight, then drain and keep in a moist cloth for 1-2 days until sprouted.
Boil sprouted moong beans for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender but still crunchy. Drain and cool.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled sprouted moong, shredded chicken, chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, and pomegranate seeds.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and salt. Mix gently.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Vegetable and Moong Dal Khichdi
recipes.health_benefit: This one-pot meal is easy to digest, rich in complex carbohydrates and fiber from brown rice and moong dal, which can support healthy blood sugar and lipid levels. The vegetables add essential vitamins and minerals, promoting overall wellness.
instructions: Wash brown rice and moong dal thoroughly. Soak for 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds; once they splutter, add chopped onion and sauté until light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomato and cook until it softens.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Cook for a minute.
Add the chopped mixed vegetables, soaked brown rice, and moong dal. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil.

If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook for 3-4 whistles (or about 15-20 minutes on medium heat). If using a pot, cover and simmer until rice and dal are tender and water is absorbed, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with plain curd or a light pickle.

recipes.name: Fruit and Nut Lassi (Buttermilk Smoothie)
recipes.health_benefit: This lassi provides probiotics from curd, which may support gut health. The fruits add natural sweetness and fiber, while nuts contribute healthy fats (omega-3 from walnuts), potentially aiding in LDL management. It's also a good source of calcium.
instructions: Combine low-fat curd, mixed berries, banana, walnuts, ground flax seeds, and optional sweetener in a blender.
Add water or fortified milk to achieve desired consistency.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.
